items.prompt: You are finishing an expense report late at night, and padding a few receipts would be easy and probably never noticed. You start telling yourself that no one in your position could resist, and that this pressure is unlike anything anyone else faces. What does 1 Corinthians 10:13 counsel here?
options: Accept that your temptation is unique to you and too strong to resist, so a small lapse is understandable
Remember that this temptation is common to man, and that God is faithful to provide a way to escape so you can bear it
Give in this once, since God sometimes allows people to be tempted beyond what they are able to bear
Conclude that God has left you alone in this, so you must decide entirely on your own strength
items.explanation: 1 Corinthians 10:13 teaches that no temptation is beyond what is common to man, and that God is faithful and will with the temptation make a way to escape. The passage rules out both the 'unique' excuse and the idea that God allows unbearable temptation.
items.hint: The verse speaks about how ordinary temptation is and about God's faithfulness in the midst of it.

items.prompt: You run a small home bakery, and customers rarely check whether a 'one-pound' bag actually weighs a pound. Shaving a little off each order would quietly boost your profits. Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 11:1?
options: Trim the portions slightly, since customers never weigh them and no one is harmed
Keep weights honest only for regular customers who might notice
Give honest measure every time, because a just weight is the LORD's delight and a false balance is an abomination to him
Lower the weight but add a nicer label so customers feel they still got value
items.explanation: Proverbs 11:1 says a false balance is abomination to the LORD, but a just weight is his delight. Honest measure matters whether or not anyone checks.
items.hint: Think about what the verse says the LORD delights in when it comes to measuring.

items.prompt: At your office, coworkers casually take printer paper, pens and snacks home, and the amounts seem trivial. You wonder whether small things like this really matter for a person of integrity. Which response best reflects the teaching of Luke 16:10?
options: Be faithful even in these small things, because the one faithful in what is least is faithful also in much
Small items do not count; integrity only matters when large sums are involved
Take what you need now and plan to be honest later when you have more responsibility
Follow whatever your coworkers do, since shared habits cannot be dishonest
keywords: faithful in that which is least
items.explanation: Luke 16:10 teaches that he that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much, and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much. Small choices reveal and shape character.
items.hint: The verse connects how we handle little things with how we handle big ones.

items.prompt: Late in the evening you read a cutting message from a colleague, and you have a blistering reply drafted and ready to send. No one would stop you, and it would feel satisfying in the moment. Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 25:28?
options: Send it immediately, since expressing every feeling is a sign of strength
Send it but copy others so the colleague feels publicly corrected
Let your feelings have free rein tonight and deal with any damage tomorrow
Rule your own spirit and hold back, because a person without self-control is like a city broken down and without walls
items.explanation: Proverbs 25:28 compares a man that hath no rule over his own spirit to a city that is broken down and without walls. Lack of self-control leaves a person exposed and vulnerable.
items.hint: The verse uses the picture of a city's defenses to describe self-control.

items.prompt: You find a wallet full of cash in an empty parking lot, and the thought of keeping it grows stronger the longer you hold it. You catch yourself thinking, 'God must have put this in my path to test me, so it's partly on Him.' What does James 1:13-15 counsel here?
options: Treat the situation as God tempting you, so the responsibility is shared
Assume that a thought which is only entertained privately can never lead anywhere harmful
Recognize that God tempts no one; you are drawn away by your own desire, and desire that is allowed to grow brings forth sin
Keep the cash, since finding it without witnesses proves it was meant for you
keywords: drawn away of his own lust
items.explanation: James 1:13-15 says God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man; rather every man is tempted when he is drawn away of his own lust and enticed, and lust when it hath conceived bringeth forth sin. Blame cannot be shifted to God, and inner desire left unchecked grows into sin.
items.hint: The passage traces temptation to its true source and describes how it grows.

items.prompt: Weeks ago you made an error in a report that cost your team time, and no one ever traced it back to you. You could keep quiet forever, or you could come clean and change how you work. Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 28:13?
options: Confess the mistake and forsake the careless habit, for whoever confesses and forsakes their sins will find mercy
Stay silent, since covering a mistake that no one discovered is the wisest way to prosper
Quietly blame the error on a system glitch so no one is hurt
Admit it only if someone else discovers it first
items.explanation: Proverbs 28:13 teaches that he that covereth his sins shall not prosper, but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy. Concealment is the path the verse warns against.
items.hint: The verse contrasts two responses to wrongdoing and the outcome of each.

items.prompt: You work remotely, and you notice you only work hard when your manager's status shows online or a check-in call is coming up. The rest of the time you coast, confident no one can tell. Which response best reflects the teaching of Colossians 3:22?
options: Work diligently mainly when your supervisor is watching, since pleasing them is the goal of good work
Coast when unobserved, because obedience only applies to tasks someone checks
Put effort into looking busy on camera so your manager feels reassured
Work with singleness of heart, fearing God, rather than with eyeservice as a menpleaser
items.explanation: Colossians 3:22 calls for work not with eyeservice, as menpleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God. Working hard only when observed is exactly the eyeservice the verse rejects.
items.hint: Look for the unusual word the verse uses for work done only to be seen.

items.prompt: Your family is away for the weekend, and you are alone at home with a streaming service and an internet browser. Some content you would never watch in front of others is just a click away. Which response best reflects the teaching of Psalms 101:2-3?
options: Integrity is for public life; what you watch in private at home is a separate matter
Walk within your house with a perfect heart and set no wicked thing before your eyes
Watch it this once, so long as you resolve to behave wisely in public afterward
Allow yourself a little, since only outward deeds, not what you look at, can cleave to you
keywords: no wicked thing before mine eyes
items.explanation: In Psalms 101:2-3 the psalmist resolves, 'I will walk within my house with a perfect heart. I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.' Integrity is pledged specifically for private life at home and for what one chooses to look at.
items.hint: Notice where the psalmist says he will walk with integrity, and what he refuses to look at.

batch.theme: self-control, temptation and integrity when no one is watching

items.prompt: A coworker's husband died suddenly, and she now lives alone. Several weeks after the funeral, most people have stopped checking on her, and you wonder whether it is your place to reach out. Which response best reflects the teaching of James 1:27?
options: Visit her in her affliction and continue showing practical care, since caring for widows is part of pure religion
Leave her alone, because grief is private and visits only intrude
Send one sympathy card and consider your duty finished, since the funeral is over
Wait for her to ask for help, since it is not your responsibility to visit
items.explanation: James 1:27 describes pure and undefiled religion as including the duty 'to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.' Continuing to visit and care for her lives out that teaching.
items.hint: Notice what James says pure religion actively does for those who are suffering.

items.prompt: Your close friend has been caring for his elderly father, who has dementia, and he admits he is exhausted and hasn't had a break in months. You have a free Saturday each month. What does Galatians 6:2 counsel here?
options: Tell him that everyone must carry his own family problems alone
Offer to share the load, such as staying with his father so he can rest
Advise him to stop talking about his struggles so he doesn't burden others
Avoid him for a while so his stress doesn't affect you
items.explanation: Galatians 6:2 commands, 'Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.' Helping carry your friend's caregiving load is a direct application.
items.hint: The verse speaks of what believers should do with each other's heavy loads.

items.prompt: Years ago you lost your mother and were deeply comforted by friends and by your faith. Now a new colleague has just lost her mother and seems overwhelmed. Which response best reflects the teaching of 2 Corinthians 1:3-4?
options: Keep your own loss to yourself, since past sorrow should never be revisited
Tell her that her grief is smaller than yours was, so she should cope
Use the comfort you received from God to comfort her in her trouble
Avoid her until she is feeling better, since comforting is for professionals
keywords: comfort them which are in any trouble
items.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:4 says God comforts us 'that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.' Your past comfort equips you to comfort her.
items.hint: Paul explains a purpose behind the comfort God gives us.

items.prompt: At a community meeting, an elderly neighbor slowly rises to share a concern, and some younger attendees roll their eyes and talk over him. You are seated nearby. Which response best reflects the teaching of Leviticus 19:32?
options: Join the others in ignoring him, since older people's views are outdated
Interrupt him to speed the meeting along
Treat him as no different from a nuisance, since age earns no special regard
Show him honor and respect, giving him attention as he speaks
keywords: honour the face of the old man
items.explanation: Leviticus 19:32 commands, 'Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God.' Showing him respect reflects this command.
items.hint: The verse ties reverence for God to how we treat the aged.

items.prompt: Your widowed mother needs help with errands and household needs, but you have been pouring your time into volunteer projects across town and barely see her. You feel pulled in two directions. Which response best reflects the teaching of 1 Timothy 5:4?
options: Learn first to show piety at home by caring for your mother, repaying what your parents gave you
Focus only on outside projects, since helping family earns no credit before God
Assume someone else in the church will handle her needs, so you need not
Tell her she should manage on her own, since adult children owe parents nothing
items.explanation: 1 Timothy 5:4 says the children of a widow should 'learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God.' Caring for your mother is the priority this verse describes.
items.hint: Paul says something should be learned 'first' and where it should be practiced.

items.prompt: A friend's teenage son has died, and you go to the house unsure what to say. You feel pressure to explain the tragedy or offer advice. Which response best reflects the example of Job's friends in Job 2:11-13?
options: Explain at length why this must have happened so your friend can understand
Stay away until you have the right words, since silence is unhelpful
Come and sit with your friend in his grief, sharing quiet presence rather than many words
Quickly change the subject to lighter topics so he forgets his pain
items.explanation: Job's friends came 'to mourn with him and to comfort him' and 'sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great' (Job 2:11-13). Their silent presence is the example in this passage.
items.hint: Look at what the friends did before anyone began to speak.

items.prompt: A friend is deeply grieving a recent loss, and you plan to visit. You're tempted to arrive with upbeat music and jokes to 'snap her out of it.' Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 25:20?
options: Insist on cheerfulness, because forced joy quickly cures sorrow
Be gentle and sensitive to her heavy heart rather than pressing lighthearted cheer on her
Tell her that grieving shows weak faith and she should sing instead
Bring a group for a party so she has no time to feel sad
items.explanation: Proverbs 25:20 compares one 'that singeth songs to an heavy heart' to taking away a garment in cold weather and 'vinegar upon nitre.' Forced cheer wounds rather than comforts, so gentleness fits the moment.
items.hint: Consider the images of a removed coat in winter and a harsh reaction.

items.prompt: On the same evening, you are invited to a lively celebration with friends and to the visitation for a coworker's elderly father who has died. You're inclined to skip the visitation because it feels heavy. Which response best reflects the teaching of Ecclesiastes 7:2?
options: Choose the celebration, since feasting is always wiser than mourning
Skip both, because neither event has anything to teach you
Attend the celebration and avoid thinking about death, since it is not your concern
Go to the house of mourning, where the living reflect on the end of all men
items.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:2 says, 'It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.' Attending the visitation honors the grieving and encourages sober reflection.
items.hint: The Preacher compares two kinds of houses and says which is better.

batch.theme: grief, comfort, visiting the sick and caring for the elderly

items.prompt: You've just been promoted to lead your department, and a colleague jokes that now you'll finally have people to do your errands. You wonder what kind of leader you want to be. Which response best reflects the teaching of Mark 10:43-44?
options: See the role as a reward and expect the team to serve your needs first
See greatness in the role as becoming the team's servant and meeting their needs
Keep your distance from the team so they respect your new authority
Use the promotion mainly to get your own ideas recognized
items.explanation: Jesus taught that whoever would be great 'shall be your minister' and whoever would be chiefest 'shall be servant of all' (Mark 10:43-44). True leadership is measured by service, not by being served.
items.hint: Jesus turned the usual idea of greatness upside down.

items.prompt: A friend from your small group is overwhelmed after losing a job while caring for a sick parent. You have some free evenings and could help with meals and errands. What does Galatians 6:2 counsel here?
options: Wait for them to ask, since everyone should handle their own problems privately
Offer advice from a distance but avoid getting involved in their practical needs
Step in to help carry the load, since this fulfils the law of Christ
Remind them that hardship builds character and leave them to grow through it
items.explanation: Galatians 6:2 says, 'Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.' Practically sharing a friend's load is how believers live out Christ's law.
items.hint: The verse speaks of carrying something together.

items.prompt: Your team is choosing who will present a successful project to senior leadership, and you know you could push to take the spotlight. A quieter colleague did much of the groundwork. Which response best reflects Philippians 2:3-4?
options: Make sure leadership knows the success was mostly your doing
Stay silent and let credit fall wherever it happens to land, even if it lands on you
Insist on presenting, since visibility is important for your career
Value your colleague above yourself and look out for their interests by giving them the credit and opportunity
items.explanation: Philippians 2:3-4 teaches to do nothing 'through strife or vainglory' but in 'lowliness of mind' to esteem others better than ourselves, looking 'on the things of others.' Elevating a colleague's contribution fits that humility.
items.hint: Think about whose interests the passage asks you to look at.

items.prompt: You sit on a neighborhood council deciding how to allocate a small grant. Several low-income families who would be affected aren't at the meeting and have no one representing their needs. Which response best reflects Proverbs 31:8-9?
options: Speak up on their behalf, judge fairly, and plead the cause of the poor and needy
Stay quiet, since those who didn't attend gave up their say
Support whichever option the most influential members prefer
Postpone any decision indefinitely to avoid controversy
items.explanation: Proverbs 31:8-9 instructs, 'Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.' Those with a voice in decisions should use it for those who lack one.
items.hint: The passage tells someone in authority what to do with their mouth.

items.prompt: As a supervisor, you're frustrated that a staff member keeps missing deadlines. You're tempted to threaten their job in front of the team to scare everyone into line. Which response best reflects the teaching of Ephesians 6:9?
options: Use threats freely, since fear is an effective motivator
Treat them fairly without threatening, remembering you too answer to a Master in heaven who shows no partiality
Ignore the problem entirely so you never have to confront anyone
Be harsh with this employee but lenient with your favorites
items.explanation: Ephesians 6:9 tells masters to treat those under them well, 'forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him.' Leaders are accountable to God and must not rule by intimidation or favoritism.
items.hint: The verse reminds those in charge that they also have someone over them.

items.prompt: You've been asked to coordinate the volunteer team at your church's food pantry. You feel reluctant and wonder whether you could just give orders while others do the work. What does 1 Peter 5:2-3 counsel here?
options: Accept the role only if it brings recognition or some benefit
Take the role reluctantly and do the bare minimum because you were pressured
Run the team firmly as its boss, since volunteers need to know who's in charge
Serve willingly and eagerly, leading by personal example rather than lording it over others
items.explanation: 1 Peter 5:2-3 urges oversight 'not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind,' and not as 'lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.' Good leaders serve gladly and lead by example.
items.hint: The passage contrasts ruling over people with showing them the way.

items.prompt: As a new manager, one employee regularly brings you unflattering stories about coworkers, and you've started acting on them without checking. Office trust is souring. Which response best reflects the warning of Proverbs 29:12?
options: Keep rewarding the informer, since knowing everything strengthens your control
Refuse to listen to falsehoods and verify claims, knowing a leader who heeds lies corrupts the whole team
Share the stories more widely so everyone is aware of the problems
Treat every report as true, since employees wouldn't bother inventing them
items.explanation: Proverbs 29:12 warns, 'If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked.' A leader who welcomes falsehood encourages it throughout those under him.
items.hint: Consider what happens to those under a leader when the leader welcomes untrue reports.

items.prompt: You head a small family business through a tough season. One advisor says to rule strictly and conceal hard facts from staff; another says to be kind but always honest. Which response best reflects Proverbs 20:28?
options: Lead with mercy and truth together, since this is what upholds a leader's position
Rely on strict control and fear, since kindness looks weak in hard times
Hide the bad news to keep morale up, even if it means misleading people
Be honest but harsh, since mercy has no place in running a business
items.explanation: Proverbs 20:28 says, 'Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.' Lasting authority rests on combining compassion with honesty, not fear or deception.
items.hint: The verse names two qualities that preserve a ruler.

batch.theme: serving others, leadership and using authority well

items.prompt: Your calendar is crammed with work deadlines, family events, and volunteer commitments, and you feel guilty that you can't do everything at once. A friend suggests you simply accept that different things have their proper times. Which response best reflects the teaching of Ecclesiastes 3:1?
options: Recognize that there is a season and a time for each purpose, and give each task its proper time
Try to do every task simultaneously so nothing ever waits
Conclude that timing doesn't matter and everything should be done immediately
Drop all commitments, since no activity has a rightful place in life
items.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:1 teaches that "to every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven." Life's activities each have their fitting time, so not everything must happen at once.
items.hint: The verse speaks of seasons, not of doing everything at once.

items.prompt: It has been a frustrating week: your car needed repairs and a project at work stalled. Over dinner, you notice you've only talked about what went wrong. What does 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 counsel here?
options: Wait to give thanks until circumstances improve
Rejoice, keep praying, and give thanks in every thing
Give thanks only for the things that went well this week
Keep a careful record of complaints so you can pray about them later
items.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 says, "Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks," calling believers to gratitude in all circumstances, not only good ones.
items.hint: Notice how broadly the passage applies thankfulness.

items.prompt: At a milestone birthday, you realize years have slipped by while you've postponed what matters most to you. You want to use your remaining time well. Which response best reflects the prayer of Psalms 90:12?
options: Avoid thinking about the passing of time so it doesn't trouble you
Assume there will always be more years, so priorities can wait
Ask God to teach you to number your days so you apply your heart to wisdom
Fill every remaining day with as much activity as possible, regardless of purpose
items.explanation: Psalms 90:12 prays, "So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom." Being mindful that our days are limited is meant to lead us toward wise living.
items.hint: The psalmist wants counting days to lead somewhere.

items.prompt: You are hosting a dinner and become irritated that a relative is sitting and listening to a guest's stories instead of helping in the kitchen. You're tempted to complain publicly. What does Jesus' response in Luke 10:40-42 suggest?
options: Insist that serving is always more important than listening
Ask the guest to step in and order the relative to help
Conclude that hospitality is unimportant and should be abandoned
Notice that you may be careful and troubled about many things, while one thing is needful
items.explanation: In Luke 10:40-42 Jesus tells Martha she is "careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful," and that Mary "hath chosen that good part," sitting and hearing his word.
items.hint: Jesus did not tell the listening sister to get up.

items.prompt: You've been staying up past midnight and waking before dawn, convinced that if you just work harder you can secure everything yourself. You are exhausted and anxious. Which response best reflects the teaching of Psalms 127:2?
options: Recognize that anxious overwork is vain and that God gives his beloved sleep
Cut sleep further, since rest is a sign of laziness
Rise even earlier, because success depends entirely on your effort
Eat the bread of sorrows now so you can enjoy life later
items.explanation: Psalms 127:2 says, "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep." Sleep is a gift, not a failure.
items.hint: The verse calls one pattern 'vain' and names a gift.

items.prompt: Your team has just finished an intense stretch of serving clients, so busy that no one had time even to eat lunch. As the leader, you're deciding what to do next. Which response best reflects Jesus' words in Mark 6:31?
options: Schedule another busy stretch immediately to keep momentum
Tell everyone that rest is only for those who did less work
Invite them to come apart to a quiet place and rest a while
Praise the skipped meals as proof of true commitment
items.explanation: In Mark 6:31 Jesus told his busy disciples, "Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while," because "they had no leisure so much as to eat."
items.hint: Consider what Jesus offered people who had been coming and going nonstop.

items.prompt: You're offered a promotion with much higher pay, but it would mean constant stress, long hours, and little peace at home. Your current role pays less but leaves room for a calm life. What does Ecclesiastes 4:6 counsel here?
options: Both hands full is always better, whatever the vexation
A handful with quietness is better than both hands full with travail and vexation of spirit
Quietness only matters once you have accumulated plenty
Travail is the surest path to a peaceful spirit
items.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:6 says, "Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit," valuing peace above more gain gotten with turmoil.
items.hint: The verse compares one handful with two, and weighs what comes with each.

items.prompt: You've begun working nights and weekends purely to grow your investments, constantly watching market charts and neglecting friendships. A coworker urges you to chase wealth even harder. Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 23:4-5?
options: Set your eyes firmly on riches, since they are the most lasting thing
Trust your own cleverness to make sure your riches never leave
Labour all the harder, because wealth stays with those who pursue it
Labour not to be rich, remembering that riches make themselves wings and fly away
items.explanation: Proverbs 23:4-5 warns, "Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom," because "riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven."
items.hint: Think about the bird imagery the proverb uses for wealth.

batch.theme: rest, time, priorities, gratitude and joy

items.prompt: Your teenage nephew is living with you for a year, and you are tempted to leave his character and habits for 'life to sort out later.' You wonder whether patient guidance now really matters. Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 22:6?
options: Assume children will find their own way and that early guidance makes little lasting difference
Wait until he is an adult before trying to shape his habits or values
Leave all guidance to his school, since home life has little effect on character
Take time now to train him in the right way, trusting that early formation tends to last into later life
items.explanation: Proverbs 22:6 says to 'Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it,' so diligent guidance in youth has lasting value.
items.hint: Think about what this verse says happens 'when he is old.'

items.prompt: Your elderly parents call often, and after a stressful week you are tempted to ignore them and speak dismissively about them to friends. You want to respond rightly. What does Exodus 20:12 counsel here?
options: Honour your father and mother, treating them with respect and regard even when it is inconvenient
Honour your parents only if they have earned it by agreeing with your choices
Keep your distance, since adult children owe their parents nothing further
Speak respectfully to their faces but freely mock them to others
items.explanation: Exodus 20:12 commands, 'Honour thy father and thy mother,' attaching a promise of long days to the command, with no condition about convenience.
items.hint: This is one of the Ten Commandments, and the first word of it is a verb about respect.

items.prompt: At a community meeting, an elderly man with white hair slowly makes his way to the front, and some younger attendees roll their eyes and keep their seats. You consider how to respond. Which response best reflects the teaching of Leviticus 19:32?
options: Ignore him, since respect should be based only on someone's position or wealth
Rise and show him honour, treating age itself with respect as an act of reverence toward God
Join the others in quietly laughing at how slow he is
Offer respect only if he proves he is more qualified than the younger speakers
items.explanation: Leviticus 19:32 says, 'Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God,' tying respect for the aged to reverence for the LORD.
items.hint: The verse describes a physical action of respect toward grey hair.

items.prompt: Your mother, now in her eighties, offers advice about a family matter. Friends say her views are outdated and you should simply tune her out because of her age. What does Proverbs 23:22 counsel here?
options: Stop consulting parents once you have your own household
Listen politely only to your father, since the verse concerns fathers alone
Treat her age as a reason to dismiss her opinions
Listen to your parents and do not despise your mother because she has grown old
items.explanation: Proverbs 23:22 says, 'Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old,' forbidding contempt for an aging parent.
items.hint: Notice what the verse says about a mother's age.

items.prompt: An older volunteer at your organisation has made a real mistake, and you need to address it. A colleague suggests confronting him sharply in front of everyone so he learns his lesson. Which response best reflects the teaching of 1 Timothy 5:1-2?
options: Rebuke him harshly, since age gives no special claim to gentle treatment
Never mention the problem at all, even if it continues
Approach him respectfully and appeal to him as you would to your own father
Ask a younger staff member to scold him publicly so you are not involved
items.explanation: 1 Timothy 5:1 says, 'Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father,' calling for respectful appeal rather than harsh rebuke, and goes on to treat others as family 'with all purity.'
items.hint: The passage compares how to treat older and younger people to members of a family.

items.prompt: Your child keeps failing to finish chores, and you are frustrated. You are tempted to respond with constant belittling and harsh outbursts to 'toughen them up.' Which response best reflects the teaching of Ephesians 6:4?
options: Avoid needlessly provoking them to anger, and instead raise them with patient instruction and godly correction
Use sarcasm and ridicule, since shame is the quickest way to change behaviour
Give up on correction entirely so the child never feels upset
Let the child raise themselves, since instruction is the church's job alone
keywords: provoke not your children to wrath
items.explanation: Ephesians 6:4 tells fathers to 'provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord,' which rules out both exasperating harshness and abandoning correction.
items.hint: The verse contains both a warning and a positive instruction for parents.

items.prompt: Your aging father needs some financial help. You are tempted to tell him your money is already pledged to a religious cause, so you are excused from helping him, even though you could do both. In light of Mark 7:10-13, what does Scripture counsel here?
options: A religious pledge rightly cancels any duty to help your parents
Declaring resources set apart as a gift is a wise way to avoid family obligations
Do not use a religious vow as an excuse to neglect your parents, because that makes God's command to honour them of none effect
Honouring parents means only speaking kindly, not practical help
items.explanation: In Mark 7:10-13 Jesus rebukes those who declared their resources 'Corban' so they need do nothing for father or mother, saying this made 'the word of God of none effect through your tradition.'
items.hint: Jesus criticised a tradition that used a 'gift' to God as a loophole.

items.prompt: You are the youngest person newly appointed to lead a team, and several older members quietly doubt you because of your age. You wonder how to respond. Which response best reflects the teaching of 1 Timothy 4:12?
options: Demand respect forcefully and remind them often that you are in charge
Become an example in your speech, conduct, love, spirit, faith and purity so your youth gives no cause for contempt
Step aside, since young people should never hold responsibility
Match their attitude by dismissing the older members' contributions
items.explanation: 1 Timothy 4:12 says, 'Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity,' answering doubts through godly example rather than force.
items.hint: The verse lists areas of life where a young person should set a pattern.

batch.theme: teaching the young, honouring parents and respecting elders
